types.label: value.title
types.note: A document is a VIEW over facts — it holds only {title, summary}. Membership + order live entirely in `_doc/<docId>/<factKey>` decorations (type doc-order); a member can be ANY fact (a doc-block, a canvas `el:`, a `cell:`, a claim), so 'blocks ARE facts' (no graduation). There is no inline block array — order is one fractional-seq write per decoration.

types.label: value.id
types.note: The DEFAULT type for prose authored directly in lit (markdown + lit fences) — a convenience, NOT a requirement for doc membership. A doc is a view over facts, so any fact of any type becomes a block when a `_doc/<docId>/<factKey>` decoration places it (lit renders it via its own type's renderer). Reach for doc-block only when minting fresh prose with no better home.

types.label: value.seq
types.note: Ordering decoration. Key `_doc/<docId>/<blockKey>`; the key-encoded rule (ADR-0003) projects it into a `block inDoc doc:<docId>` Reference edge — doc membership as graph. `doc`/`block` also ride in the VALUE (2026-07-12): a nested-slug docId (`docs/architecture/adr/x`) breaks the key regex's per-segment capture, so deriveBackboneEdges falls back to these value fields when the key alone can't be parsed back apart.

schema.seq: number — narrative position (fractional, e.g. 2.25, allows insertion)
schema.doc: string — the doc slug (matches `{doc}` in the key), the fallback source for the inDoc edge's `to`
schema.block: string — the member's full fact key (matches `{block}` in the key), the fallback source for the inDoc edge's `from`

types.label: value.title
types.note: A daily log — the chronological spine (Karpathy's log.md; ADR-0040). Keyed `log:<YYYY-MM-DD>`: a thin day fact that the day's captures tag and link `on`. lit renders it as the day's captures in temporal order (a view over the day, not a doc with membership). Holds {date, week, month, year, title} for navigation. Owned by lit (the wiki/render layer); written by @c15r/input (the intake organ) — complementary without coupling, the contract is the fact + the `on` edge.
